recipes.name: New York Cheesecake
ingredients_raw: 3 (8 ounce) packages cream cheese, room temperature

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
Make crust: Mix together graham crumbs, melted butter, and sugar in a medium bowl until evenly moistened. Press into the bottom and 1/2 inch up the sides of a 9-inch springform pan. Set aside.
Make cheesecake: Mix together cream cheese and sugar in a large bowl with an electric mixer until smooth. Blend in eggs, vanilla, and cream of tartar. Pour over crust in the pan.
Bake in the preheated oven until the center is set, about 50 minutes. Allow to cool on the counter for 5 minutes.
While cheesecake is cooling, make topping: Mix together sour cream, sugar, and vanilla in a medium bowl until smooth.
Pour topping over cheesecake, starting from the sides of the pan and working your way to the center.
Return cheesecake to the oven until topping is set, about 5 minutes. Allow to cool in the pan to room temperature. Chill in the refrigerator for at least 6 hours before serving.

raw_recipe.headline: New York Cheesecake
raw_recipe.description: This New York cheesecake recipe with sour cream topping features a buttery graham crust and a creamy, silky smooth texture that's irresistibly good.

review.reviewBody: I have been making this recipe for a while now and I must admit it's become my favorite. I think it's involved but oh so worth it. Sometimes I like to add a hint of almond extract in the sour cream topping. This is the one time I allow myself to splurge on such a decadent dessert. I would give this more than 5 stars if possible because it is THE BEST!

After experimenting a few times I found it best to line spring form pan with parchment paper and use a stand mixer on #4 speed and the paddle head from start to finish. All ingredients room temp and softened. Mix cream cheese for about 8-10 mins until smooth, add sugar and continue to let it mix for 5 mins, add vanilla and cream of tartar and mix for 2 mins - scrape sides and bottom of bowl occasionally between additions. Here's the delicate part: While continuing to mix, (with all eggs in measuring cup or bowl) add/spill in eggs one at a time as you see the yolk pop and blend add the next - DO NOT OVER MIX - once you add the forth egg use a baking spatula to scrape down side and turn off mixer. Use spatula to scrape and fold mix from bottom of bowl. Pour into crust prepared pan. Bake for 50 mins following remaining instructions to sour cream. After baking sour cream on for 5 mins, let sit for one hr in pan then remove clasp and use a knife or large icing spatula to run underneath entire cake. Grip pan on one side and help cake off pan with knife or spatula on the other side onto a plate or board. The cake will be a bit flexible which helps the transfer yet but can damage if you drop on plate - glide it down closely to plate.

If in a hurry, microwave the three cream cheese on a plate for 45 secs, then mix for 10 mins until creamy and smooth. For the eggs, soak in hot water for one to two mins then take out.

This is a world class cheesecake recipe. Guys! Instead of almond extract try adding a 1/2 tsp of lemon or lime zest to the sour cream topping, and a 1/2 tsp of lemon or lime juice to the cream cheese filling. You'll thank me later. Also, a 1/4 tsp of cinnamon to the graham cracker crust really enhances the flavor. The cheese cake can cool for up to 15 minutes after you pull it out of the oven the first time. And the sour cream topping should bake for 10 minutes, not 5. It'll set perfectly in the fridge. :-)

This recipe was so amazing! I followed the recipe exactly but put the cheesecake in a water bath to bake (use a crockpot liner around the cheesecake to keep it water tight). It took about 1 hr 5 minutes in my oven before I put the topping on. This is a keeper!

This is the best recipe! I've made two strawberry cheesecakes, and making a raspberry one today. I used half the amount of sugar, and combined 1/2 cup homemade strawberry jam into the cream cheese. Topped each slice with a spoonful of jam. It went so fast I had to make the second one!
I’ve made this three times and all three times it’s been great. My secret is I never cook it at 3:50. I cook it 320 for 50 minutes in water a bath and yes, you need cream of tartar.

I baked it at 400 degrees for 15 minutes and then reduced it to 200 degrees for an additional 35 minutes. I took it out at that time and frosted it with the sour cream and baked it for an additional 10 minutes. I left it in the oven with the heat turned off until cooled and then refrigerated. I topped it with a raspberry pie filling and fresh raspberries. The sour cream topping was a perfect foil for the sweet topping. Will absolutely make again.

This cheesecake has been a HUGE hit each time I’ve made it! I receive text messages from friends afterward raving about it! The fun thing to do with this one is mix up the crust. I’ve used crushed peanut butter sandwich cookies, crushed peppermint Oreos and even fruity pebbles. I’ve also swirled blueberry reduction into the sour cream layer before baking. Adds a really fun look and subtle blueberry flavor. Also, one addition; I don’t feel this cheesecake is in need of a water bath (honestly I think it should be a last resort anyway, but that’s me). I’ve found usually splitting is a result of over whipping while adding the eggs. Adjust that first before doing a water bath. Or don’t. It’s just one humans opinion 😁 I just made a peanut butter swirl version! Swirled a peanut butter sauce I make through the sour cream top. Was the best cheesecake I have ever made. Ever.
Replaced the milk with cream, baked the cheesecake with oven door slightly ajar, and there were no cracks at all! Very pleased with the results

I've been using this recipe for several years. I've won two blue ribbons at the state fair with it. I've had people pay me to make one for them. Out of all the cheesecakes I make, and there are several, this is the most requested. I use half vanilla extract and half vanilla bean paste, both for the filling and the topping. Also, I make a warm lemon blueberry topping that people love. Really, it doesn't need anything. It's delicious!
Love this recipe. I cook it using a pan of water in the oven this time. No cracking. It came out beautiful.

I found this recipe a couple years ago and it is now what I have to make for any parties I go to. The only adjustment I have made is to use Dominican White Vanilla. It takes the flavor to another level!!!

It was delicious!!!!There should have been a mention that it would have been helpful to either have a water bath or a tray underneath the springform pan. The butter from the graham cracker crust leaked all over the oven and burned. At that point there should have been an adjustment to the temperature of the oven to accommodate the pan/waterbath. I will have to wait the several hours to see how this cheesecake tastes.

Cream of tartar should be mixed into the egg whites and then that mixture folded into the cream cheese mixture. If you add the cream of tartar directly to the cream cheese mixture, you’ll end up with lumps from curdling.
I started making this exact recipes a few years ago for family parties and now I’m not allowed to show up without it. I’ve made it countless times and now have to make more than one.
By far, the best tasting and most flavorful cheesecake I have EVER had in my 72 years on this planet. Just incredible!!!
Delicious! No need to change anything about the recipe.

Thank you for sharing this recipe. I made it for Father's day because my husband wanted a New York style cheese cake. We really loved it! I honestly thought that the frosting sounded weird, but decided to try it anyways. Oh my goodness it was excellent and it may become my new frosting for cookies also. It almost has a lemony flavor.

I made this yesterday. I did not make the topping because my husband wanted a fruit topping instead. The cheesecake came out nice and tasty. The reason for the four stars is because the crust is way too sweet. Next time I make this, I will add a lot less sugar to the crust and make the sour cream topping. Thanks for this nice recipe. I can see me making this one often.
Easy recipe. Always turns out well. I use a tsp of lemon juice instead of cream of tartar.
